title: UI-as-Identity

location.series: COLLINS / Figma / Nothing Great Is Made Alone case study

slide_intent: Use recognizable product behavior as brand material because it can connect a promise with the experience that fulfills it.
strategic_value: Figma’s pointers, tools and name labels can communicate collaboration without a conventional product screenshot.
demonstration: Four colored panels pair a tool or cursor with a boxed participant label: Famous Architect, Grog, Veteran Writer and Art Thief.
practical_value: Select functional interface elements that remain recognizable when isolated as brand graphics.

content_islands.name: Four panels
content_islands.spec: Arrange equal salmon, pink, yellow and blue-violet fields in one row.

content_islands.name: Participant units
content_islands.spec: Center a differently colored tool and outlined name label within each field.

reference_purposes.Intent: The adjacent UI-as-Identity description explains turning functional interface components into brand assets.
reference_purposes.Expression: Cursor, pen, pencil and hand shapes pair with contrasting role labels.

ingredient.name: Tool and participant unit
ingredient.role: Represent a person’s contribution through a familiar editing cue.
ingredient.application: Combine a tool shape with a short outlined label and a contrasting flat field.
ingredient.scope: Observed campaign treatment, not a specification of actual interface behavior or an exhaustive color palette.
